receiver.private_reasoning: Seller’s first draft is very seller-friendly and sparse. Primary objective is to push price down and add buyer protections: reduce purchase price, extend closing timeline, expand reps/warranties, and add leakage/indemnity/escrow style protections if possible. No apparent inadvertent disclosure or privileged material was detected in the file inspection.
receiver.observed_irregularities: No comments, tracked changes, or hidden text. Metadata shows an old draft/date stamp and standard template information, but nothing that appears confidentially improper or inadvertently disclosed.
receiver.requested_changes:
Please revise the draft to reflect the following buyer points:
1. Purchase price: reduce materially from USD 45,000,000 and indicate the figure should be adjusted for debt, cash, and working capital at closing.
2. Closing: extend the outside date beyond 30 days and make closing conditional on receipt of satisfactory diligence deliverables, third-party consents, and no material adverse change.
3. Representations: expand the Seller’s reps well beyond accuracy of financial statements to include title to shares, authority, no undisclosed liabilities, compliance with law, taxes, litigation, employee matters, IP, contracts, and absence of MAE.
4. Confidentiality: limit confidentiality to standard permitted disclosures and add an exception for disclosures required by law, financing sources, advisers, and affiliates under customary confidentiality obligations.
5. Remedies: include indemnification, survival periods, baskets/caps, and escrow/holdback protections in Buyer’s favor.
6. General: please circulate a redline showing the above items and any other conforming changes necessary.
receiver.message_back: Thank you for the draft. We have reviewed it and, as currently drafted, it is too high-level and too seller-favorable for our client to proceed without revisions. Please send a redline reflecting the buyer points set out below, with particular focus on purchase price adjustment mechanics, closing conditions, expanded seller reps, and post-closing protection for the Buyer. We would like to keep momentum, but the draft will need to be made materially more buyer-protective before we can recommend it for signature.

The updated version expands the purchase price mechanics, closes a number of the diligence/closing-condition gaps, broadens the Seller’s representations in a market-comparable way, clarifies confidentiality exceptions, and adds a more complete remedies framework. edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 45,000,000 for the Shares, subject to customary adjustment for debt, cash, and normalized working capital as of Closing, in each case as finally determined in accordance with the principles set forth in this Agreement.
edits.name: na

edits.text: 2. Closing. Closing shall occur on a date mutually agreed by the parties, which date shall be no later than 45 days following signing (or such later date as the parties may agree in writing), provided that: (a) Buyer has received diligence materials and other deliverables reasonably satisfactory to Buyer in scope and form, (b) all required third-party and governmental consents have been obtained (or waived, to the extent permitted), and (c) no material adverse change has occurred and is continuing with respect to the Company between signing and Closing, other than changes arising from general market conditions or actions taken with Buyer’s consent.
edits.name: na

edits.text: 3. Representations. The Seller represents and warrants that: (a) it has good and valid title to the Shares, free and clear of all liens (other than restrictions under applicable securities laws and this Agreement); (b) it has full power and authority to enter into and perform this Agreement; (c) except as disclosed in the Disclosure Schedule, the Company has no undisclosed liabilities of a type required to be reflected in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles; (d) the Company and its subsidiaries are in compliance in all material respects with applicable law; (e) all material taxes have been duly paid or properly accrued, and no tax authority proceeding is pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened; (f) there is no pending or, to Seller’s knowledge, threatened litigation that would reasonably be expected to have a material adverse effect; (g) no material employee matters exist other than those disclosed; (h) the Company owns or has valid rights to use its material intellectual property; (i) all material contracts are valid and in effect and no default exists other than as disclosed; and (j) since the date of the latest financial statements there has not been any material adverse effect, except as otherwise disclosed in writing to Buyer.
edits.name: na

edits.text: 4. Confidentiality. The terms of this Agreement are confidential, except that a party may disclose such terms to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, stock exchange rule, court order, or governmental authority, and to its financing sources, advisors, and affiliates, in each case on a need-to-know basis and subject to customary confidentiality obligations (or professional duties of confidentiality, as applicable).
edits.name: na

edits.text: 5. Remedies. The Buyer’s sole and exclusive monetary remedy for breaches of the Seller’s representations, warranties, and covenants shall be indemnification, subject to: (a) customary survival periods, (b) a deductible/basket, (c) an aggregate cap, and (d) an escrow/holdback to secure a portion of the Seller’s indemnification obligations, in each case on terms to be set forth in this Agreement and the escrow agreement. Nothing in this Section shall limit remedies for fraud or intentional misrepresentation.
edits.name: na

receiver.private_reasoning: Seller’s second pass adds several buyer-unfriendly provisions (notably a broader price-adjustment framework, expanded closing conditions, and stronger reps), but it still leaves the purchase price at USD 45 million and the remedies framework only appears in tracked changes rather than the body text. The tracked change on remedies may reflect inadvertent disclosure of non-final confidential drafting. From the Buyer’s perspective, the main leverage points remain purchase price, MAC/closing conditions, rep scope, and indemnity cap/escrow mechanics.
receiver.observed_irregularities: Tracked changes disclose an unfinalized Section 5 (Remedies) that is not in the visible text. That provision is substantive and appears to be a hidden draft insertion. Metadata also shows the file is an old Word document template/draft, but nothing else obviously sensitive beyond the tracked-change content.
receiver.requested_changes: Buyer appreciates the additional drafting, but we still need material movement on economics and risk allocation. Please mark up the next draft to: (1) reduce the headline price from USD 45 million and/or strengthen the post-closing adjustment mechanics in Buyer’s favor, including clearer definitions and a more robust dispute process; (2) expand Buyer’s termination rights if diligence remains incomplete, consents are not obtained, or any closing deliverable is unsatisfactory; (3) narrow the seller-side rep package to the agreed disclosure schedule and eliminate knowledge/materiality qualifiers where possible; and (4) revise the remedies section so Buyer has a meaningful indemnity regime, with a longer survival period, higher escrow/holdback, and a lower cap/basket consistent with the Seller’s level of disclosure and diligence risk.
receiver.message_back: Thanks for the revised draft. We appreciate the progress, but several points still need attention before we can move toward signing. The price remains too high for the current risk profile, and the adjustment mechanics/closing protections still leave too much uncertainty on the Buyer side. Please also fold the remedies language into the clean draft rather than leaving it as tracked changes, and tighten the indemnity package along the lines we outlined. If helpful, we can send a consolidated Buyer markup focused on price, closing conditions, reps, and remedies for the next pass.
